name: Tobias Kettlesworth
equipment: A collection of Wonderland tales (handwritten manuscript, his life's work)
A costume (a patchwork cloak of many colors)
A letter of recommendation from a grateful audience (now useless in Wonderland)
A small notebook for recording new stories
A jar of pickles (12) — travel snack
features: Lucky (when rolling a natural 1 on an attack, ability check, or save, can reroll and must use the new roll)
Brave (advantage on saves against being frightened)
Halfling Nimbleness (can move through the space of any creature that is of a size larger than yours)
Naturally Stealthy (can attempt to hide when obscured by a creature at least one size larger)
Bardic Inspiration (d8 — bonus action to inspire an ally within 60 ft., grants d8 to add to one ability check, attack roll, or save within 10 minutes; CHA modifier uses per short rest — 4 uses)
Jack of All Trades (add half proficiency bonus to any ability check that doesn't already include proficiency bonus)
Song of Rest (during short rest, allies who spend Hit Dice regain an extra 1d6 HP)
Font of Inspiration (Bardic Inspiration recharges on short rest)
Bonus Proficiencies (3 additional skill proficiencies — History, Insight, Deception)
Cutting Words (use reaction and expend Bardic Inspiration to subtract d8 from a creature's attack roll, ability check, or damage roll)
Additional Magical Secrets (learn 2 spells from any class — Counterspell, Spiritual Weapon)
By Popular Demand (Entertainer feature — can find a place to perform for free lodging and food, and gain local fame)

personality.traits: I collect stories the way a dragon collects gold — compulsively, jealously, and with great delight. I narrate my own actions in third person when excited. I am simultaneously the bravest and most frightened person in any room — brave because I cannot resist a good story, frightened because I understand exactly how stories end for people like me.
personality.ideals: Stories. Every life is a story, every battle is a chapter, every choice is a plot twist. The best stories are the ones where ordinary people do extraordinary things — and right now, I am IN one of those stories. I refuse to let it end badly.
personality.bonds: I have spent my entire career collecting tales of Wonderland — interviewing travelers, transcribing oral traditions, and piecing together the truth behind the legend. My manuscript, 'The True Tales of Wonderland,' is my life's work. When the looking glass opened, I realized every story I'd collected was real. I have to see this through — not just for the adventure, but because the ENDING of this story matters, and right now it's heading toward tragedy.
personality.flaws: I cannot resist a dramatic moment, even when drama is tactically inadvisable. I have been known to pause mid-combat to compose a verse about what's happening. I am also terrified of the Queen of Hearts specifically because I know her story — I know what she does to people, I've catalogued it in excruciating detail, and the gap between 'reading about decapitation' and 'being decapitated' is uncomfortably narrow.

appearance: A small, round-faced halfling standing 3'2" with warm brown skin, a riot of curly chestnut hair, and bright hazel eyes that are always wide — either with wonder, terror, or both simultaneously. His face is expressive and mobile, shifting between emotions with the speed of a stage actor (which he basically is). He has a button nose, slightly crooked from an incident involving a particularly aggressive puppet show, and smile lines that suggest a life spent laughing. He wears studded leather armor beneath a magnificent patchwork cloak of dozens of different colored fabrics — each patch represents a different story or song in his repertoire. His lute, 'Curiosity,' is slung across his back — it's a well-loved instrument with carved halfling designs and a small brass plate reading 'Property of T. Kettlesworth — if found, I'm probably dead, please return to the Prancing Pony.' He carries a worn leather satchel stuffed with notebooks, loose pages, and a handwritten manuscript that represents fifteen years of Wonderland research. He moves with the quick, bouncy energy of a halfling who has had too much tea and not enough sleep.
backstory: Tobias 'Toby' Kettlesworth has been a storyteller since before he could properly read — which, given that he grew up in a halfling community where stories were currency, meant he was wealthy by age six. He traveled the world as an itinerant bard, performing in taverns, courts, festivals, and campfires, collecting tales from every culture he encountered. But one category of story captured his imagination above all others: tales of Wonderland. He first heard the name from a gnomish librarian who dismissed it as 'a fey fairy tale about a fairy tale' — which was exactly the kind of recursive nonsense that Toby found irresistible. He began collecting every reference to Wonderland he could find: a dwarven miner's account of a tunnel that 'went sideways into somewhere wrong,' an elven poet's ballad about 'the land where ravens are desks and desks are ravens,' a human scholar's treatise on 'autonomous demiplanes with ludic properties.' Over fifteen years, Toby assembled the most comprehensive collection of Wonderland lore in the material plane — hundreds of fragments, quotes, legends, and eyewitness accounts (the eyewitnesses were mostly considered insane, which Toby found only added to their credibility). He was writing the introduction to his definitive manuscript when word reached him that a looking glass had been discovered in a ruined tower — a glass that matched every description of the Wonderland portal he'd ever collected. He arrived at the tower breathless and trembling with excitement. When the glass activated and pulled him through, his last thought before tumbling into Wonderland was: 'THIS IS GOING TO MAKE A FANTASTIC CHAPTER.' He has since revised this assessment to 'THIS IS GOING TO KILL ME AND IT WILL MAKE A FANTASTIC POSTHUMOUS CHAPTER.' But he wouldn't leave for anything in the world. He's inside the story now, and the story needs a narrator.
